path: Healey, new in post, faces an OBR shortfall; Treasury briefs options including CGT alignment while No 10 worries about markets and investor backlash.
Pre-budget leaks steer toward reliefs, allowance and property tweaks; backbenchers push CGT equalisation; officials warn rate rises raise little and may cut receipts.
Budget on Oct 28 tightens reliefs and freezes thresholds but leaves headline CGT rates unchanged; a narrow rate change on a niche asset class remains possible.
Boebert campaigns for re-election in a safe seat; leadership discourages any departure given the narrow majority.
No scandal or appointment emerges; she continues media appearances and campaign stops.
She stays on the ballot and in office through the deadline; no resignation announcement.
SNS floods media and patronage networks; students campaign in cities; established opposition parties partly run separately, splitting anti-SNS votes.
Polls show a close race; SNS mobilises rural and public-sector voters; fraud allegations over voter rolls intensify.
On Oct 25 SNS list narrowly tops the seat count; students second and strong; protests follow allegations of irregularities.
Democrats lead aggregated Senate-control odds after favourable red-state polling; GOP spends heavily in toss-ups.
Late October polls show some GOP consolidation in Texas, Ohio, Iowa; odds narrow but Democrats stay ahead most hours.
Before Nov 3 the race tightens near even; a brief GOP lead for four straight hours is possible but not the base case.
White House focuses on midterms; AARO continues routine work; congressional UAP caucus presses for releases.
No executive action on UAP; ODNI declassification push stays on other historical files.
Window closes Oct 23 without a clear new release, though a small AARO case publication remains possible.
Midterm environment favours Democrats; the Democratic nominee invests in DFW suburbs; the GOP nominee relies on suburban Republican habit.
Denton polling tightens; college-educated ticket-splitters lean against the GOP nominee, especially if it is Paxton.
On Nov 3 the Republican carries Denton by a few points; a strong wave would be needed for a flip.
Democrats are modestly favoured; GOP odds sit around 40-45% on aggregate markets.
Red-state polling moves both ways; a bad news cycle for Trump pushes GOP odds down toward mid-30s.
A late GOP partial rebound keeps odds above 30%; sustained four-hour dip below 30% would require a big shock.
Gyurov leads the field; GERB, PP-DB and Revival field rivals, fragmenting the vote.
Election fatigue keeps turnout expectations near 40%; Gyurov polls well short of a clear majority of a high-turnout electorate.
On Oct 25 Gyurov finishes first but turnout and share fall short; a runoff is set for Nov 1.
Vance holds a wide lead in 2028 nomination markets; Trump keeps succession ambiguous.
Midterm campaigning keeps Vance prominent; Rubio and Trump Jr. trail well behind.
On Oct 31 noon Vance remains the top-priced option.
Eby calls a snap vote on favourable polling; Conservatives struggle with defections and a right-wing splinter.
NDP campaign leads; vote-splitting on the right costs Conservatives suburban ridings.
On Oct 24 NDP wins the most seats; Conservatives hold Interior base but finish second.
Eby's NDP enters the snap election ahead; Conservatives are divided.
Campaign remains a two-party contest; a late Conservative surge is possible but limited by splits.
NDP most likely finishes first, not second; NDP second only if Conservatives win outright.
Yamanaka's resignation triggers a short campaign; parties sort out endorsements; Harasawa's backing is unclear.
LDP-Komeito and opposition camps consolidate around preferred candidates; name recognition matters in a low-turnout race.
On Oct 18 the endorsed frontrunner wins; Harasawa's chance depends on whether she holds a major-party endorsement.
Gyurov leads; GERB, PP-DB, Revival field separate candidates, fragmenting opposition.
Runner-up likely the GERB-backed candidate around 20%; Gyurov polls in the 35-45% range.
On Oct 25 the margin over second lands somewhere 10-30 points; 20-30 band is one of several plausible outcomes.
Flávio leads market odds narrowly; first round Oct 4 tests both camps.
First-round results show Lula ahead; traders reprice, eliminated candidates' endorsements split.
Odds swing close; Lula may overtake for several hours, but right-wing consolidation can keep Flávio ahead.
Midterm campaign proceeds; white non-college voters remain strongly Republican.
Democratic gains among college-educated whites narrow but do not erase the GOP edge.
CNN House exit poll on election night shows Republicans winning white voters by high single to double digits.
Polarised SNS vs students race drives mobilisation by both camps; diaspora return campaigns launch.
Inflated voter rolls with many emigrants cap measured turnout despite intense engagement.
Official turnout rises above 2023 to roughly 60-66%, short of 70%.
SNS and Student List dominate; SPS and opposition lists run separately or jointly.
SVM holds its steady minority vote around five to six seats.
At least one other list (SPS or an opposition list) wins more seats; SVM finishes fourth or lower.
Student List campaigns as main challenger; some opposition parties run separately.
SNS state resources hold its floor near 40%; students compete for anti-SNS votes.
Students win a large share but well below 50% of valid votes.
Trump travels frequently for midterm stops and possibly a foreign trip; White House rotates pool slots.
CNN remains in the rotation intermittently despite spats.
A CNN reporter likely joins at least one Air Force One flight before Oct 31 unless excluded after a feud.
Kotlikoff runs Cornell amid an emerging controversy; trustees signal support.
No federal ultimatum demanding leadership change materialises in the window; faculty grumble but do not force exit.
He remains president through Oct 31.
Saudi Arabia holds the co-pilot; Israel investigates motive; UAE seeks jurisdiction.
Without diplomatic ties, Riyadh avoids transferring to Israel; talks focus on UAE or home country.
By Oct 31 the co-pilot stays in Saudi custody or goes to UAE; no transfer to Israel.
Syria-Israel security talks continue via envoy Barrack; no leader-level event scheduled.
Possible milestone prompts a call, but routine contacts handled by envoys.
No confirmed Trump-Sharaa conversation by Oct 31 in the base path; a call around a deal remains plausible.
Flávio campaigns in the runoff protected by parliamentary immunity.
STF and PGR avoid actions that look like election interference.
No charge or arrest by Oct 31.
Lula campaigns on Northeast programmes; Flávio courts evangelicals.
Lira's machine helps Flávio but Calheiros mobilises for Lula.
Lula carries Alagoas comfortably on Oct 25.
Amapá narrowly backed Bolsonaro in 2022; Alcolumbre's ties to government add a pro-Lula pull.
Evangelical base keeps Flávio competitive.
Close result; Flávio slightly favoured to carry the state.
Amazonas split narrowly in 2022; Manaus leans right, interior leans Lula.
Both campaigns target Manaus; small national swing decides it.
Near coin-flip result on Oct 25.
Barbalho machine mobilises for Lula; Flávio strong in agribusiness south.
Lula keeps a margin in Belém and the northeast of the state.
Lula carries Pará; Flávio wins only with a large national swing.
Tarcísio endorses Flávio; Lula strong in the capital.
Interior delivers a solid right-wing margin even with lukewarm Tarcísio effort.
Flávio carries São Paulo on Oct 25.
Diaspora votes split: Europe for Lula, US and Japan for Flávio.
Turnout drives the outcome; US-based mobilisation by the right is possible.
Close exterior result; roughly a coin flip with slight Lula lean based on 2022.
US maintains pressure on cartels; Venezuela post-Maduro authorities cooperate; Mexico rejects troops.
Possible US strike or joint raid on land in Venezuela or Colombia; Mexico remains off limits.
A confirmed qualifying land action occurs only if Washington escalates; base path is maritime strikes only.
